title: Profiling CPU and Allocations
description: Use dotnet-trace, dotnet-counters, and Visual Studio diagnostics to profile CPU usage and garbage collection allocations in ASP.NET Core applications.

data.text: CPU profiling tells you which methods consume the most processor time. Allocation profiling shows where objects are created and how often the garbage collector runs. In ASP.NET Core, high allocation rates increase GC pause times, which directly hurts request latency and throughput.

`dotnet-trace` collects CPU samples from a running .NET process with minimal overhead. You can analyze the trace with Visual Studio, `dotnet-gcdump`, or PerfView to see which methods are hot. Look for tight loops, LINQ queries over large collections, and recursive algorithms.

data.title: Collecting a CPU Trace
data.content: Run these commands in a terminal to collect a 30-second CPU profile from a production-like environment.
data.code:
# Collect a CPU trace for 30 seconds
dotnet-trace collect \
  --process-id 1234 \
  --providers Microsoft-DotNETCore-SampleProfiler \
  --duration 00:00:30 \
  -o cpu.nettrace

# Convert to a speed scope format for browser viewing
dotnet-trace convert cpu.nettrace --format speedscope

data.text: `dotnet-counters` monitors live processes for GC heap size, allocation rate, and time in GC. A high allocation rate means the GC is working harder and may pause threads. Focus on Gen 0 and Gen 1 collections; Gen 2 collections indicate long-lived objects or large object heap fragmentation.

terms.definition: The number of bytes allocated per second. High rates increase GC frequency and pause times.
A full garbage collection that examines all managed objects and is the most expensive pause type.
Memory allocated for objects larger than 85,000 bytes. LOH is only collected during Gen 2 GCs.

data.title: Monitoring GC and Allocations
data.content: Use dotnet-counters to watch GC metrics in real time while generating load against your API.
data.code:
dotnet-counters monitor \
  --process-id 1234 \
  System.Runtime \
    GC Heap Size \
    Gen 0 GC Count \
    Gen 1 GC Count \
    Gen 2 GC Count \
    Allocation Rate

rows: Live GC, memory, thread pool metrics

data.title: Avoid Debug Builds
data.text: Always profile Release builds with optimizations enabled. Debug builds allocate more, inline fewer methods, and produce misleading CPU profiles. Enable ReadyToRun and tiered compilation for the most accurate picture.

Common allocation culprits in ASP.NET Core include string concatenation in loops, boxing value types, capturing variables in LINQ closures, and returning large anonymous objects from API endpoints. Use `ArrayPool<T>` and `Memory<T>` to reduce allocations in high-throughput paths.

data.title: Key Takeaway
points: Use dotnet-trace for CPU hot paths and PerfView or Visual Studio for deep dives.
Use dotnet-counters to watch allocation rate and GC pause times in real time.
Profile Release builds with optimizations enabled for realistic data.
Focus on Gen 2 collections and high allocation rates before micro-optimizing individual lines.
data.takeaway: If you cannot measure it, you cannot improve it. Start with the lowest-overhead tool that answers your question.
